newsitem.title: USA: S.C. teacher who wrote on child back to work.
newsitem.headline: S.C. teacher who wrote on child back to work.

text.p: A white teacher who wrote "Where are my Glasses!" on a black student's face two months ago returned to school Wednesday despite protests.

First-year kindergarten teacher Phyllis Adelsflugel was suspended without pay Nov. 14 for writing on 5-year-old Nina Campbell's face the day before. Her return was allowed on condition that she complete sensitivity training and send a written apology to Nina and her family.

Adelsflugel said she wrote on Nina after the child repeatedly forgot to bring her eyeglasses to school. But Nina's mother alleged racism, saying the teacher would not have done the same thing to a white child.

Some residents were not satisfied with the punishment. About a hundred people protested her return Wednesday, including members of the local National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People (NAACP), the nation's oldest civil rights group.

"We're protesting to show that Nina Campbell is the victim and not the teacher," said Ed Bryant of the North Charleston branch of the NAACP. "Reinstating the teacher was not the right decision. We felt it was capricious."
Nina was transferred from Pepperhill Elementary school to another Charleston County school shortly after the incident.
